brief.ask: Art-direct "Harvest Wheatfield Sunset" — #11 of the 72 Ambo church visualizers (Calm Contemporary Worship lyric visualizer, Collection I of 72; subgenre Scenic Nature). Premise: Multi-plane bearded golden wheat stalks swaying beneath a warm amber-rose sun. Backlit bearded wheat stalks with delicate awns sway in two depth planes against a glowing harvest sunset, responding smoothly to acoustic guitars and vocals. Lighting today: Key: Golden hour 3300K sunset low on the horizon; warm rim light on grain. Service use: Thanksgiving, stewardship, communion (Bread of Life), acoustic sets. Audio mapping today: Swell → Sways backlit golden wheat stalks in unison; Vocal → Blooms warm sunset rim-light across the horizon; Shimmer → Releases floating golden pollen motes. Palette: #1C1018 #5E2B38 #E08E45 #FFEAB3. Keep the id, name, premise and palette; rebuild the direction: the geometry and depth planes, typography for the worship lyric band (one line at a time, four to five seconds a line, word-by-word progression), image logic (how the procedural scene (no concept plate: the plate is generative, in code) and the procedural scene meet), texture, motion, and which audio channel drives what. Decide it — the lead's lens will drive the kit's material weave and optical pass for this one.
brief.audience: Congregations watching a projector or LED wall from the pews, five to forty metres away, eyes on the words; and the worship leader or volunteer running Ambo live from a laptop.
brief.feeling: Stillness and reverence — a sanctuary that breathes with the singer's voice; gorgeous, slow, never a screensaver.
constraints: Build method (fixed): a real-time Canvas 2D audio-reactive renderer in Plajah's worship visualizer kit — sanctuary background, multi-plane depth (god rays, motes, bokeh), the kit's Council optical pass (35mm light leaks, anamorphic flare, film grain, colour punch, and a tactile material weave keyed to the LEAD director's lens) and the kit's lyric / scripture typography engine. No video playback, no WebGL, no assets beyond the one concept plate.

Audio drives amplitude, colour, light, growth and glow only — never the position of the words. Envelopes are smoothed; nothing strobes or flashes (photosensitive-safe); uptempo pulses are spring-damped.

The reading band is sacred: lyrics or scripture must stay legible at 1920×1080 and 4K from the back pew, over the busiest moment of the scene. A text-safe dimming band is part of the kit; direct how the scene yields to it.

Typefaces are fixed to the kit's open-licensed set: Noto Serif (text serif), Outfit / Inter (sans), Cinzel (display), JetBrains Mono. Direct scale, case, tracking, measure and hierarchy, not new families.

Sacred imagery is used correctly and respectfully: biblical places and objects are specific and attributable, never costume; nothing denominational or branded; nothing that reads as a music video or a screensaver.
Runs at 60 fps on an integrated-GPU laptop driving a projector: favour layered gradients, cached textures and a few large shapes over particle storms.
Keep this visualizer's id, name, premise and four-colour palette. The council owns the direction, not the catalogue entry.
references: No concept plate: the scene is built entirely in code from the premise.
Sample lyric lines on the band: "Be still my soul the Lord is on thy side" / "Bear patiently the cross of grief or pain".

proposals.title: Cantus Firmus of the Field
proposals.idea: A φ-governed luminance spine runs from soil to sky before any stalk is drawn, and every element — wheat plane, rim glow, pollen mote, lyric band — earns its vertical position by derivating from that single primary measure, so the scene reads as one resolved composition rather than layered decoration.
proposals.geometry: A golden-ratio spine is computed at render-init: canvas height H, φ = 1.61803. Horizon line sits at H/φ from the bottom (≈ 61.8% up). Sky zone occupies the upper 38.2%; earth zone the lower 61.8%. Within the earth zone a second φ-subdivision places the foreground wheat root line at H/(φ²) from the bottom (≈ 23.6%). Three vertical luma bands divide the width: left edge, φ-midpoint (W/φ), right edge — these three columns govern where sway amplitude peaks and where rim-light blooms are permitted. The text-safe dimming band occupies a horizontal strip from 14% to 34% of canvas height, centred on the lower-sky zone just above the horizon; it is declared as a no-draw exclusion zone for all procedural geometry before any stalk or glow is placed. God-ray shafts originate from a single vanishing point locked to the φ-intersection of the horizontal spine and the left luma band, fanning at angles t
proposals.typography: Cinzel Regular, sentence-case, for the lyric line — not all-caps, because Cinzel's capitals carry enough mass and the lowercase descenders give the line breath and humility appropriate to worship. Base size: 4.2% of canvas height at 1080p (≈ 45px), scaling linearly to 4K. Tracking: +0.04em — open enough to survive projection bloom but not so wide it dissolves into the scene. Lyric line centred horizontally, baseline resting at 26% of canvas height (inside the text-safe band, 4px above the dimming band's lower boundary). Word-by-word reveal: each incoming word fades in over 180 ms with a subtle upward translate of 4px, settling to rest; the completed line holds at full opacity; outgoing line dissolves over 240 ms with no translate — it simply recedes. No bounce, no scale pulse, no colour shift on audio — the words do not perform. A scripture or reference attribution, when present, sits tw
proposals.imageLogic: There is no concept plate. The scene is entirely procedural. Sky is a two-stop radial gradient: #1C1018 at zenith, transitioning through #5E2B38 at mid-sky, arriving at #E08E45 at the horizon band — the gradient origin is the vanishing point, not the canvas centre, so the glow is structurally earned rather than cosmetically centred. The horizon band itself is a narrow luminance spike (8px feathered to 40px) of #FFEAB3 at full opacity, simulating the compressed colour of a low sun without drawing a disc that would compete with the lyric. Wheat stalks are procedurally generated Bezier curves: each stalk is a cubic with root fixed on the foreground or midground baseline, a control point at 60% of stalk height offset laterally by a per-stalk phase-varied sine, and a terminal awn cluster of three to five short strokes diverging at 12–18° — all stroked in #E08E45 with opacity varying by depth
proposals.texture: The material weave is parchment-and-linen: a base noise pass (8×8 tileable Perlin noise computed once at init, cached as an offscreen canvas) is composited over the sky zone at 'multiply' blend, opacity 0.09, giving the gradient the tooth of a sized paper without adding visual noise that competes with the lyric. Over the wheat planes, the same noise tile is composited at 'overlay', opacity 0.06, so the stalks read as having surface rather than being vector graphics. The anamorphic streak is a single horizontal line 1px tall, centred on the horizon luma spike, extending 60% of canvas width symmetrically from the vanishing point, rendered as a linear gradient from transparent through #FFEAB3 at 0.55 opacity to transparent — forbidden from entering the text-safe band. Film grain is a per-frame additive noise pass at σ=3.2, opacity 0.04, applied last over the entire canvas before the optical
proposals.motion: Sway (Swell → amplitude): Both wheat planes sway via a per-stalk sine function. Each stalk has a base phase offset (assigned at init, uniform-random within its plane's phase window). Swell amplitude is smoothed with a 180ms attack, 400ms release envelope. At rest (amplitude 0) the foreground stalks move ±2.5° from vertical; at full swell ±7°. Midground stalks move at 62% of foreground amplitude and 1.15× the period, so the two planes never lock in unison — they breathe in counterpoint. The sway period for foreground is 3.8s; midground 4.4s. These are not tempo-synced; they are slow enough to read as wind, not as a beat. Rim-light bloom (Vocal → glow): The horizon luma spike width expands from 8px to 28px feather and its opacity climbs from 0.85 to 1.0 over a 220ms attack, 600ms release, driven by vocal amplitude. The sky gradient's mid-stop (#5E2B38) shifts 4% toward #E08E45 at peak voca
proposals.productionMethod: Real-time Canvas 2D renderer. Init phase (runs once, ~12ms): compute φ-spine constants, generate stalk array (root x, phase, depth-plane, awn angles), rasterise the 8×8 Perlin noise tile to an offscreen canvas, compute the bokeh ellipse positions from φ-grid intersections. Per-frame draw order (60fps target, integrated GPU): 1. Sky gradient (fillRect + radial gradient, one call). 2. Horizon luma spike (fillRect + linear gradient). 3. God rays (4–6 semi-transparent triangles from vanishing point, globalAlpha 0.07). 4. Midground stalk array (strokePath, cached Bezier params updated per-frame for sway). 5. Foreground stalk array. 6. Bokeh ellipses (pre-positioned, opacity modulated by swell). 7. Pollen motes (active list, max 40 live at once). 8. Noise texture composite (drawImage offscreen, multiply, sky zone clip). 9. Text-safe dimming band (fillRect, #1C1018 at 0.38 opacity, covering the
proposals.humanTrace: The stalks are not uniform: at init, each stalk's root x is jittered ±6px from an even grid, its height varies ±12% from the plane mean, and its awn count (3–5) and awn angles are individually randomised within the botanical range — the field reads as observed, not tessellated. The Perlin noise tile was authored by directing the generator with a low frequency (0.08 cycles/px) and high persistence (0.62) to approximate the irregular tooth of a cold-pressed watercolour paper rather than digital smooth noise. The horizon luma spike's feather width is asymmetric: 6px above, 14px below, because a setting sun compresses its light more tightly above the line than below — that asymmetry is a physical observation built into the constant, not a stylistic choice.
proposals.risk: The risk is austerity at the moment of congregational emotion. A φ-governed field with no disc, no burst, no dramatic reveal asks the viewer to find the beauty in proportion and breath rather than spectacle. The Baroque Dramatist will say the reveal never announces itself and therefore never arrives; I will hold that the earned luminance bloom on the vocal is the announcement, and that it lands harder because the scene has been disciplined enough to deserve it. The risk is worth it because worship visualizers that perform too hard become the thing people watch instead of the words they are meant to speak.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want the sun to rise or crest or pulse — a legible arc of drama with a clear climax. I argue that a scene structured around φ-proportion and a cantus firmus horizon already has its climax built in: it is the moment the vocal bloom widens the rim light and the congregation feels the field open without anything moving toward them. proposals.title: Ink Pressed Into Grain
proposals.idea: A woodblock-register imperfection baked into every procedural wheat stalk and lyric letterform makes the screen read as a thing printed on light rather than displayed through it.
proposals.geometry: Two depth planes: NEAR stalks occupy a horizontal band from 58% to 92% of canvas height, spaced on a jittered 11-column grid with ±4% horizontal drift baked at scene init — positions do not change after that, they are pressed once, like a plate; FAR stalks run 38% to 65% height on a 17-column grid with ±2% drift, taller but lighter. No symmetry axis. A single horizon line sits at 34% from top — low and committed, not centered. God-ray origins are declared at scene init from three fixed polar coordinates (azimuth 218°, 231°, 247° from left edge, elevation 12°) and never move; audio scales their opacity, not their angle. The lyric band occupies 68%–88% of height — a strip low enough that the sky and far stalks breathe above it.
proposals.typography: Noto Serif, weight 400, sentence case only — no caps, no display face; this is a field journal entry, not an announcement. Single lyric line, 3.8vw at 1080p, scales to 2.8vw at 4K to hold measure. Tracking: 0.04em — tight enough to feel hand-set. Word-by-word reveal: each incoming word fades in over 180ms with a +1.5px vertical offset that eases to 0 — like a stamp landing. Active word carries a 0.06em underline in #E08E45 at 60% opacity; previous words drop to 72% white. The text-safe dimming band is a gradient-masked rect: #1C1018 at 64% opacity from 66% to 92% height, with a 6% feathered top edge — dark enough to read over any stalk density, present enough to feel like a page rather than a caption box. No scripture reference on the lyric band; it sits as a plain line. Cinzel and JetBrains Mono are held in reserve for chapter/verse overlays only and are not used here.
proposals.imageLogic: No concept plate. The scene is entirely procedural. Stalk silhouettes are Bezier paths: three-segment spine from base anchor to tip, with two control handles that carry the sway. Awn geometry is a fan of 6–9 line strokes per stalk head, length scaled to stalk tier (near: longer, far: shorter). At scene init, each stalk is assigned a base hue offset drawn from a narrow band ±8° around #E08E45 and a fixed luminance jitter ±12% — this is the pressed-plate moment, the one human editorial decision that cannot be undone by the renderer. The sky is a three-stop radial gradient: #FFEAB3 at the horizon origin, #E08E45 at 40% radius, #5E2B38 at 85%, #1C1018 at canvas edge. God rays are drawn as low-opacity (#FFEAB3, 8–14% alpha) radial wedges from the three declared polar origins, cached to an offscreen canvas on init and composited with 'screen' blend. Bokeh motes are 28 circles maximum, radius 4
proposals.texture: The kit's material weave for this lens is a woodblock-grain overlay: a 512×512 tileable noise field generated once at load via a simplex pass with frequency 0.018 and 3 octaves, rendered to an offscreen canvas, then composited over the full scene at 18% opacity using 'multiply' blend — this is what makes the sky feel pressed rather than rendered. Film grain is the kit's standard per-frame noise pass at 6% opacity, seed incremented each frame. The 35mm light-leak pass is a single warm horizontal streak (#FFEAB3, 22% opacity, 'screen' blend) positioned at 31% from top — one pixel band, 4px Gaussian blur, static. It does not pulse. Anamorphic flare fires only when vocal amplitude crosses 0.72 threshold: a 1px horizontal line, #FFEAB3, 9% opacity, full canvas width at horizon height, 2-frame fade-in, 800ms decay — slow enough to read as light, not as a flash.
proposals.motion: Swell (low-frequency amplitude, smoothed 120ms): drives unison sway of both stalk planes. Near stalks: ±3.2° rotation from base anchor, 1.4s sinusoidal period per stalk with ±0.3s phase offset baked at init. Far stalks: ±1.6°, 1.9s period. Swell also scales god-ray opacity linearly from 6% (silence) to 14% (peak). Vocal (mid-frequency RMS, smoothed 80ms): blooms the horizon gradient — at zero vocal, the radial gradient stops at 40% radius; at peak vocal it expands to 58% radius over 600ms eased out-cubic, retreats over 1200ms. Vocal also lifts the ambient luminance of far-plane stalks by up to +18% — they glow as the voice rises. Shimmer (high-frequency transient, smoothed 40ms): releases bokeh motes from their seeded positions — at zero shimmer, motes are invisible; each shimmer pulse increases their opacity to 55% over 60ms, decays over 1800ms. Mote radius breathes ±1.5px in sync with
proposals.productionMethod: Canvas 2D renderer, 60fps target on integrated GPU. Scene init: declare all stalk positions, hue offsets, phase offsets, god-ray angles, bokeh seed positions — these are the press marks, written once. Per-frame: clear, draw sky gradient, composite woodblock texture (offscreen canvas, cached), draw god-ray wedges (offscreen canvas, cached, opacity updated), draw far stalks (Bezier paths, sway angle from swell envelope), draw near stalks, composite film grain (noise pass, cheap), draw bokeh motes (circles, shimmer envelope), draw light-leak streak (static offscreen canvas), draw anamorphic flare if vocal threshold crossed, draw lyric band (gradient rect + Noto Serif text, word state from lyric engine). All offscreen canvases are 512px or smaller and reused. Stalk count: 17 far + 11 near = 28 Bezier paths per frame — well within integrated GPU budget. No particle system. No WebGL.
proposals.humanTrace: The woodblock-grain noise overlay and the per-stalk hue/luminance jitter are both baked at scene init from a seed the director sets editorially — change the seed, get a different press run. The stalk positions, god-ray angles, and bokeh seed grid are declared constants in the source, not generated at runtime — they are the equivalent of a registration mark, a prior physical commitment. The anamorphic flare is keyed to a threshold a human decides, not to a beat grid. The lyric stamp animation (word landing with vertical offset) simulates the pressure of type on paper. None of this is decorative texture applied after the fact; each mark answers a declared prior decision.
proposals.risk: Noto Serif at sentence case in a worship context reads quiet to the point of plainness — some operators will want Cinzel and all-caps because that is what looks 'churchy.' Refusing that trades immediate recognisability for something that feels like a field Bible rather than a broadcast graphic. The woodblock overlay at 18% multiply risks muddying the warm palette on low-contrast projectors — the palette is already dark at the edges. Worth it because the alternative is a gradient sunset that is indistinguishable from a screensaver, which is exactly what this brief says it must not be. The material weave is the difference between a thing printed on light and a thing displayed through it.

arguesWith.why: The Minimalist will strip the woodblock overlay, the god-ray wedges, and the bokeh motes as surplus evidence and call what remains cleaner and more reverent. I hold that removing every mark removes the making, and a blank gradient sky is not reverence — it is absence. proposals.title: Field as State Machine
proposals.idea: The wheat field is a live simulation whose every parameter — stalk lean, rim-light radius, pollen mote density — is a direct function of the audio envelope, so the scene has no idle state: it is always reading.
proposals.geometry: Two stalk planes defined by a parametric row system: foreground plane at y=0.58–1.0 (12 stalks, spacing=viewport_width/13, scale factor 1.0), background plane at y=0.38–0.72 (22 stalks, spacing=viewport_width/23, scale factor 0.62, opacity 0.55). Each stalk is a cubic Bézier whose control-point lateral offset is the sole variable driven by audio. The horizon sits at y=0.42. Sun is a radial gradient centred at (0.5, 0.42), inner radius 4 vh, outer radius 38 vh — not a disc, a pressure zone. The sky fills y=0 to y=0.42 with a four-stop gradient: #1C1018 at apex, #5E2B38 at mid-sky, #E08E45 at horizon, #FFEAB3 at the sun core. No decorative geometry is placed without a functional state attached to it.
proposals.typography: Noto Serif, sentence-case, weight 400. Single lyric line centred at x=0.5, y=0.82 (above the foreground stalk crowns). Cap-height: 5.2 vh at 1080p, scales to 5.2 vh at 4K (absolute vh lock, not px). Tracking: 0.04em. Measure: max 22 characters per line (brief specifies four to five words per line; the engine wraps at that measure). Word-by-word progression: each incoming word fades in at opacity 0 → 1 over 180 ms (ease-out cubic), previous words remain at full opacity — the line accumulates left to right, never disappears mid-line. At line-end the full line holds 400 ms then cross-fades out over 300 ms while the next line's first word fades in. No motion on the word's spatial position — only opacity state changes. Text-safe dimming band: a vertical-gradient fill rect from y=0.72 to y=1.0, #1C1018 at 72% opacity, painted before every text drawCall. This band is fixed — it does not pulse w
proposals.imageLogic: No concept plate. The scene is entirely procedural. Stalk geometry: each stalk is drawn as a stack of four cubic Bézier segments, base to head, with a procedurally-varied width taper (base 3.2 px → tip 0.8 px at 1080p). Awn cluster at the head: six line segments per stalk, each 8–14 px, fanned ±28° from vertical, opacity 0.6. Stalk fill: vertical linear gradient #E08E45 → #FFEAB3, with a right-edge highlight strip 2 px wide at #FFEAB3 opacity 0.9 — this is the rim-light, always on. The rim-light strip width is a direct output of the vocal amplitude envelope (resting 2 px, peak 6 px, spring-damped τ=0.18 s). Background stalks use the same rule at 0.55× strip width. Pollen motes: pool of 48 cached mote objects (not spawned per frame). Each mote is a radial gradient circle, r=2–5 px, #FFEAB3 core, transparent at 1.4r. Mote y-velocity is a fixed slow drift (−0.15 px/frame). Mote opacity is g
proposals.texture: Film grain is the kit's optical pass: a 256×256 tileable noise canvas pre-rendered on init, scrolled by (1,1) px per frame, composited over the full viewport at globalAlpha 0.028 with 'overlay' blend. This is the material weave keyed to the Futurist lens: grain is not nostalgia here — it is a sampling artifact that proves the renderer is reading a live signal, not replaying a recording. No linen, no paper tooth, no analog warmth affectation. The colour punch pass: a single full-viewport rect in 'multiply' blend at #E08E45, opacity 0.07, painted last before the lyric band — this unifies the stalk and sky colour temperature without adding draw calls. Anamorphic flare: one horizontal lens streak through the sun centre, drawn as a 4 px tall rect spanning full width, #FFEAB3 opacity 0.18, painted on the offscreen god-ray canvas at init.
proposals.motion: All motion is a function of a smoothed audio envelope, never a timeline. Three envelopes: swell (low-frequency RMS, τ=0.4 s), vocal (mid-frequency RMS, τ=0.22 s), shimmer (high-frequency RMS, τ=0.12 s). Stalk sway: foreground stalk Bézier control-point offset = swell_amplitude × 18 px, applied as a sinusoidal phase offset across the stalk row (phase = stalk_index × 0.31 rad) so stalks do not move in lockstep — a travelling wave. Background stalks: same rule, amplitude × 11 px, phase offset × 0.19 rad, 80 ms lag introduced by a secondary smoothing pass. This lag is the depth cue — it is not decorative. Rim-light bloom: vocal_amplitude drives rim-light strip width (2–6 px) and sun gradient outer-radius (38–46 vh), both spring-damped. Pollen gate: shimmer_amplitude above 0.12 sets mote pool to active; below, motes fade. God-ray opacity: swell_amplitude × 0.14. All envelopes are clipped to [
proposals.productionMethod: Canvas 2D renderer, 60 fps requestAnimationFrame loop. Init pass (runs once, off main thread if OffscreenCanvas is available): (1) draw god-ray + anamorphic flare composite to 1920×1080 offscreen canvas; (2) draw 256×256 grain tile; (3) compute stalk geometry arrays (x positions, phase offsets, width tapers) for both planes and cache as typed arrays. Per-frame draw order: sky gradient → sun radial gradient → god-ray composited image (drawImage, 'lighter') → background stalks (Bézier draws, 22 stalks) → foreground stalks (12 stalks) → grain tile (drawImage, 'overlay', offset++) → colour-punch rect → text-safe dimming band → lyric text → optical pass rect (multiply). Total draw calls per frame: approximately 40 (stalks dominate). All stalk Bézier control points are recomputed from cached arrays + current envelope value — no object allocation per frame. proposals.humanTrace: The stalk phase-offset array (stalk_index × 0.31 rad) was derived by ear from observing real wheat field video — the 0.31 value is not mathematically optimal, it is the number that produced a wave that felt like wind rather than a metronome. That editorial decision — choosing 0.31 over 0.25 or 0.5 — is the human trace. The rim-light strip width range (2–6 px) was set by rendering test frames at 1080p and judging at what width the highlight reads as a physical rim rather than a glow effect. These are perceptual calibrations made by looking, not by formula.
proposals.risk: The scene has no painterly warmth, no textural comfort, no visible craft surface — it is a field of rules. In a sanctuary context this risks reading as cold or technical to a congregation expecting the visual language of harvest abundance. The risk is worth taking because the alternative — a pre-baked amber glow that does not respond — is a screensaver, and a screensaver is a lie about the moment. A field that breathes with the singer's voice is more reverent than a beautiful static image, even if it is less immediately gorgeous. The 2-px residual sway at silence is the insurance: the system never looks dead.

I reject this because a worship visualizer is not a film score: the congregant is reading words, not watching a show. Every dramatic surge competes with the lyric band for attention. proposals.title: Field Light, Named and Held
proposals.idea: Every layer of the procedural wheatfield is a documented place — the geometry derived from documented Galilean grain-belt sightlines, the amber gradient seeded from a declared 3300K colour-science origin — so that provenance and generation are the same act, not sequential obligations.
proposals.geometry: Two explicit depth planes coded as separate Canvas 2D layers: Plane A (near, z=0.72) holds seven to nine taller stalk columns at 68–84 px base width, planted on a weighted-random but fixed-seed horizontal register that does not shift between frames — permanence, not drift. Plane B (far, z=0.38) holds twelve to fifteen finer stalks, 30–44 px base width, drawn with a slightly cooler amber tint to enforce aerial recession. A horizon band sits at exactly 34% from the bottom edge (≈367 px at 1080p) — low, as a Galilee harvest sun genuinely sits in October late afternoon — not centred, not symmetrical. Above the horizon: a radial gradient sky dome. Below the horizon: a dark-amber ground plane, 6% lighter than #1C1018, suggesting soil without illustrating it. God rays are four to six diverging trapezoids anchored to the solar origin point, blended with 'screen' globalCompositeOperation at opaci
proposals.typography: Noto Serif for every lyric line — weight 400, italic, set at 3.2 vw (≈61 px at 1080p), which reads at 40 m from a pew. Line-case: title case, never all-caps — Cinzel reads as monument; Noto Serif italic reads as breath. Tracking: 0.04 em, just enough to open the grain without loosening the word. Word-by-word reveal: each word fades in over 180 ms with a 60 ms stagger between words — no slide, no bounce, only opacity — so the line assembles the way a phrase is sung, syllable by syllable. The full line holds for the remaining duration of its 4–5 s window, then dissolves in 320 ms before the next line begins. Scripture attribution (when present) set in Outfit Regular, 1.4 vw, 0.12 em tracking, right-aligned inside the same band, appearing 400 ms after the lyric line is complete. Text-safe band: a vertical gradient from rgba(28,16,24,0) at y=0.68 to rgba(28,16,24,0.72) at y=0.76, always rend
proposals.imageLogic: No concept plate, no photograph, no scan. The scene is entirely procedural. Stalk geometry: each stalk is a Bézier spine computed from a fixed-seed LCG per stalk index — the seed is declared in the config object as FIELD_SEED: 7341 and is never randomised at runtime, giving the operator a stable, repeatable scene. The awn cluster at each stalk tip is six to eight short line segments radiating from the terminal node at angles between 18° and 52° from vertical, lengths drawn from a Gaussian distribution μ=22px σ=6px — mimicking the actual awn geometry of Triticum aestivum, the species grown in the Jezreel Valley, which is the specific place this palette and light temperature reference. Bokeh motes: circles, r=3–9 px, rendered with radial gradients from rgba(255,234,179,0.7) to rgba(255,234,179,0), positioned only above the horizon line, their x,y seeded from the same FIELD_SEED so they do
proposals.texture: Three texture passes, all generative, all pre-baked at init into offscreen canvases to protect 60 fps: (1) Grain canvas 128×128, Gaussian noise, globalAlpha 0.032, tiled. (2) Vignette canvas full-resolution radial gradient from transparent centre to rgba(28,16,24,0.44) at corners — the darkening is not decorative, it draws the eye inward to the word. (3) Horizon haze: a 1920×120 px horizontal gradient from rgba(224,142,69,0.18) to transparent, positioned at the horizon band, blended 'lighten' — it gives the backlit stalks a warm atmospheric base without a photograph. The stalk fill itself is a per-stalk vertical linear gradient: root colour rgba(94,43,56,0.9) rising to rgba(224,142,69,1.0) at 60% height, then to rgba(255,234,179,0.95) at the awn tip — backlit, as the brief demands, not front-lit.
proposals.motion: Three audio channels, each mapped to one and only one visual parameter, smoothed with an exponential envelope τ=0.18 s to prevent strobing. Swell (low-frequency amplitude 20–200 Hz, normalised 0–1): drives stalk sway angle. Near-plane stalks swing ±6° from rest; far-plane stalks swing ±3.5° with a 140 ms phase lag — the lag is not randomised, it is a fixed physical constant, because wind arrives at a far plane later. Sway is a sine function of time modulated by the swell envelope; at zero amplitude the stalks are not motionless — they hold a resting oscillation of ±0.8° at 0.3 Hz, because a harvest field is never truly still. Vocal (mid-frequency amplitude 200 Hz–3 kHz): expands the radial gradient of the sun origin point from r=140 px at rest to r=220 px at full vocal, and simultaneously increases the opacity of the god-ray trapezoids from 0.09 to 0.14 — the rim light blooms with the si
proposals.productionMethod: Canvas 2D, no WebGL, no video, no external assets. Init sequence: (1) Seed LCG with FIELD_SEED: 7341, generate stalk register (x, base-width, z-plane, phase-offset) for both planes. (2) Pre-bake grain canvas, vignette canvas, horizon haze canvas into offscreen ImageData objects. (3) Compute stalk tip positions and store as a typed Float32Array for mote spawn lookup. (4) Declare solar origin as const SOLAR = {x: 0.62, y: 0.34} — a fixed, named point, not randomised, because this light has a declared origin. proposals.humanTrace: The FIELD_SEED is declared as a human editorial decision in the config — the operator can change it and the field changes, but the default is chosen because its stalk register produces a natural-looking left-of-centre density that frames the lyric band without crowding it. The solar origin at x=0.62, y=0.34 is an editorial choice derived from the actual azimuth of an October late-afternoon sun in the Jezreel Valley at roughly 32.6° N — not arbitrary, not centred. The awn geometry parameters (18°–52°, μ=22 px) are drawn from a botanical description of Triticum aestivum ear structure. These three declared origins — seed, solar position, awn geometry — are the human trace: a maker made a choice, named it, and it is legible in the config file.
proposals.risk: The risk is that specificity reads as lecture. Naming the Jezreel Valley and Triticum aestivum in the config comments means nothing to the volunteer running Ambo on a Sunday morning, and if the visual result looks like any other amber-wheat screensaver, the provenance work is invisible. That risk is worth taking because the alternative — a generic 'harvest field' that borrows the warmth of a specific geography without naming it — is the exact flattening this lens exists to resist. The specificity lives in the code, not in the worship experience; it disciplines the makers, not the congregation.

proposals.title: Light Breaking From Within
proposals.idea: A harvest field that breathes like a living organ pipe — every sway, every bloom of rim-light, every drifting mote conducted by the singer's voice so that the congregation feels the wheat field is singing back.
proposals.geometry: Three depth planes stacked on a low horizon at 28% from the bottom edge — far plane: a soft gradient sky dome collapsing from #1C1018 at zenith to #E08E45 at the horizon line; mid plane: a procedural wheat silhouette band, stalks generated as bezier curves with bearded awn tips, swaying on individual phase offsets; near plane: larger, darker foreground stalks with visible awn geometry, bokeh-softened at their roots. God rays originate from a declared point source 18% right of center at the horizon, fanning at 6–9 degree intervals across the full frame width. The lyric band occupies the bottom 22% of the frame, resting below the mid-plane wheat line so the wheat crowns frame the words from above — the field leans over the text like a nave vault.
proposals.typography: Noto Serif — lyric lines set at 4.2vw, sentence case, tracking +20, centred measure capped at 72 characters. Word-by-word reveal: each incoming word fades in over 6 frames (100ms) at full opacity while all prior words in the line hold at 85% — the newest word is always the brightest object in the band. Line transitions: outgoing line drops to 0% opacity over 18 frames with a 4px upward drift; incoming line rises from 6px below over 18 frames. Scripture attribution, when present, sits two baseline-grid units below in Cinzel, 1.6vw, tracked +80, small-caps, at 55% opacity. No weight shift, no size jump — rhythm is carried entirely by opacity and the 6-frame arrival pulse.
proposals.imageLogic: No concept plate. The scene is entirely procedural: sky is a four-stop radial gradient recomputed each frame against the vocal amplitude envelope — at peak vocal the gradient warm band widens 8% toward zenith, at silence it contracts back. Wheat stalks are bezier curves with parametric awn branches; the mid-plane stalks number 40–60, near-plane 12–18, each assigned a unique sway frequency between 0.15 and 0.45 Hz. Rim-light on individual stalks is simulated as a gaussian glow on the right-facing bezier edge, its width keyed to the vocal channel. God rays are drawn as radial gradient wedges with low alpha (0.04–0.09 per ray) composited in screen blend mode — they pulse 15% in opacity on swell. Bokeh motes in the near plane are cached circles, 8–24px, with a soft radial gradient fill; their drift velocity is constant (very slow upward float, 0.3–0.8 px/frame) and their number is fixed at 1
proposals.texture: The kit's material weave for this lens is: simulated linen grain — a static noise texture at 3% opacity over the full frame, giving the projected image the feeling of light falling on woven cloth rather than a screen. Film grain layer runs at 0.8% opacity, refreshed every 3 frames (not every frame — cost saving). A single anamorphic lens streak, horizontal, originates from the declared sun point, at 6% opacity, in #FFEAB3, clipped to the upper two-thirds of the frame so it never crosses the lyric band. 35mm light leak: a warm amber vignette edge, strongest bottom-left and top-right corners, at 10% opacity, static — it does not animate. These four passes compose the optical character: cloth, grain, flare, leak. None of them animate independently; they are the room the drama lives in.
proposals.motion: Three motion channels, each owned by one audio input. SWELL channel → unison sway amplitude of all wheat planes: at rest, peak sway angle ±3 degrees; at full swell, ±9 degrees. All stalks move in the same wind direction simultaneously (unison, not random) — this is the congregational breath, not a weather simulation. Spring-damped with 0.18 stiffness, 0.72 damping — no overshooting. VOCAL channel → two simultaneous events: (1) the radial gradient warm band on the sky widens upward, simulating the sun rising slightly into the frame — maximum 8% vertical extension over the full dynamic range; (2) the rim-light glow width on mid-plane stalk right edges increases from 2px to 9px. Both envelopes are smoothed over 120ms. SHIMMER channel → mote release: each shimmer transient above threshold adds one mote to the near-plane pool (max 18 total); motes drift upward and slightly right at constant v
proposals.productionMethod: Canvas 2D real-time renderer. Sky: fillStyle radial gradient, recomputed each frame (cheap — one gradient call). Wheat stalks: pre-computed bezier path objects stored in an array, translated and rotated each frame by a sine function seeded to each stalk's phase offset — no path recalculation, only transform. Awns: short static bezier branches, drawn relative to stalk transform — cost is minimal. God rays: drawImage of a cached off-screen canvas (rendered once at load) composited with globalAlpha adjusted per frame — zero per-frame draw cost for the ray geometry. Bokeh motes: cached off-screen circle gradients, drawImage per mote per frame — 18 drawImage calls, negligible. Linen grain: single static ImageBitmap generated at load via a seeded noise pass, composited at 3% opacity. Film grain: one 256×256 noise tile, randomly offset every 3 frames, composited at 0.8%. Anamorphic streak: one
proposals.humanTrace: The sway frequencies (0.15–0.45 Hz) and the god-ray fan angles (6–9 degrees) were chosen by ear and eye against reference footage of actual harvest fields at golden hour — they are not computed optima, they are editorial selections. The decision to run the warm band expansion on the vocal channel rather than the swell channel is a timing judgment: a voice deserves the sky, not the wind. The linen grain texture amplitude (3%) was calibrated against a projected test at 15 metres — the grain is perceptible at reading distance, invisible at the back pew. These are the hands in the work.
proposals.risk: The risk is that unison sway — all stalks moving together — reads as mechanical or naïve to an operator who expects randomised wind simulation. The counter-argument is that this is a sanctuary, not a field documentary: the congregation is not watching weather, they are breathing together, and the wheat should breathe with them. The single declared motion rhythm is the dramatic contract. If it is broken by randomised phase variation it becomes a screensaver. The operatic choice is the one that looks like a decision.

arguesWith.why: The Minimalist will argue that 18 bokeh motes, linen grain, film grain, an anamorphic streak, and a light leak are four passes too many — that one texture is discipline and four are decoration. I reject this cleanly: each of these four passes answers a different phenomenological problem. The grain gives the projection the feeling of a material surface. The streak tells the eye where the sun lives.

proposals.title: One Stalk, One Breath
proposals.idea: Strip the wheatfield to its irreducible grammar — two depth planes, one luminance threshold, one contrast — so the silence between the stalks is as load-bearing as the stalks themselves.
proposals.geometry: No horizon clutter. A single vertical axis divides the canvas at the golden ratio (0.618 from left). Foreground plane: three to five large bearded stalks, procedurally placed, occupying the lower 55% of frame height, their awns reaching no higher than 72% — above that is reserved silence. Background plane: a soft-focus field of seven to nine stalks rendered at 40% opacity and 6px gaussian blur, offset 18% right of the foreground axis, giving parallax depth without crowd. The lyric band occupies the upper 28% of the canvas — that silence is not empty, it is load-bearing negative space. No god-ray fans, no radial burst geometry: the only directional light is a single low elliptical gradient anchored at the horizon, luma-capped at 0.82 so it never bleaches the stalks into decoration. The text-safe dimming band is a 180px tall rectangle of #1C1018 at 68% opacity, feathered 32px at its top ed
proposals.typography: Noto Serif for every lyric line. 52px at 1080p, scaling to 88px at 4K. All caps suppressed — sentence case only, because all-caps at distance reads as announcement, not breath. Tracking: +0.04em. Line measure: 72% of canvas width, centred on the vertical axis. Word-by-word progression: each word fades in at 220ms opacity ramp, previous words hold at full opacity — no sliding, no kinetic push, no bounce; the line accumulates like light entering a room. Between lines: 600ms of full silence — the completed line holds, then dissolves at 400ms. The active word carries a 1px hairline underline in #E08E45 at 60% opacity; this is the only typographic gesture. Scripture attribution: Noto Serif Italic, 28px, #FFEAB3 at 55% opacity, 18px below the lyric band, never competing.
proposals.imageLogic: No concept plate. The scene is entirely procedural Canvas 2D. Background sky: a four-stop radial gradient from #5E2B38 at the horizon origin to #1C1018 at the top edge, with a secondary elliptical warm core in #E08E45 centred 12% above the bottom edge, radius 38% of canvas width — this is the sun, implied, never drawn as a disc. Stalks are procedural bezier curves with three control points each; awn geometry is a fan of eight lines radiating from the tip node at 4–9° spread, 18–26px length, rendered at 1.2px stroke weight in #FFEAB3 at 75% opacity. Bokeh motes: a pool of 28 motes maximum (not 200 — 28), radii 3–9px, drawn as filled circles in #FFEAB3 at 12–22% opacity, positions seeded from a deterministic noise field so they never cluster at the axis. The luminance gate: no mote may be placed where the background gradient luma exceeds 0.72 — they live only in the darker upper field and
proposals.texture: The optical pass contributes one layer of 35mm grain — a pre-generated 512×512 tileable noise texture in #FFEAB3 at 6% opacity, screen-blended, static (not animated per frame, cached once). No anamorphic flare geometry. One very faint light-leak: a horizontal band, 8px tall, 100% canvas width, #E08E45 at 9% opacity, positioned at exactly the horizon line — a single breath of warmth, not a performance. Film grain is the only texture. The material weave keyed to this lens is linen: the stalk stroke weight varies ±0.3px per stalk per frame via Perlin noise at 0.4 Hz — not shimmer, not flutter, the almost-imperceptible irregularity of a hand-woven thread.
proposals.motion: Swell (amplitude envelope, smoothed 180ms): foreground stalks sway on a sine curve, ±2.8° rotation around a pivot at 85% of stalk height (the base, not the centre — stalks bend from the ground). Period: 3.2s at rest, compressing toward 2.6s at peak swell. Background stalks sway at 0.7× the foreground amplitude with a 0.4s phase lag — parallax is temporal, not just spatial. Vocal (RMS of vocal band, 800Hz–3kHz, smoothed 240ms): the horizon ellipse luma ramps from base 0.62 to a ceiling of 0.82 — warm rim light blooms across the stalks, never above 0.82 luma so the sky does not bleach. Shimmer (high-frequency energy above 6kHz, smoothed 120ms, spring-damped τ=0.8s): releases between zero and four new bokeh motes per trigger into the permitted luminance zones; existing motes drift upward at 0.3–0.6px/frame and fade out over 4–7s. At silence: all motes already in flight complete their arc; n
proposals.productionMethod: Canvas 2D renderer, 60fps target. Sky gradient: createRadialGradient, two stops, drawn once and cached as an offscreen canvas, composited each frame. Stalks: procedural bezier paths, drawn each frame with transform rotation applied to a saved matrix at the pivot point. Awns: pre-computed line arrays per stalk, rotated with the stalk matrix. Grain texture: pre-generated ImageData, drawn as a single drawImage call at screen-blend composite operation. Mote pool: object pool of 28 slots, no garbage collection per frame. All audio envelopes: single-pole IIR lowpass (α derived from smoothing time and frame rate). Lyric engine: the kit's existing word-by-word fade system, no modification — only the typographic parameters above are directed. Total draw calls per frame: under 12. Runs on integrated GPU.
proposals.humanTrace: The stalk pivot point at 85% of height is a field observation: wheat bends from the culm node near the base, not from its centre of mass. The awn fan angle of 4–9° is measured from reference photographs of Triticum aestivum in late summer. The linen weave in stroke-weight variation at 0.4 Hz is physically bounded and falsifiable — if you sample the stroke width at 10Hz you will catch it drifting. The horizon light-leak at 9% opacity is the one gesture I would defend for an hour: it is the difference between a sky that was rendered and a sky that was photographed through a window.
proposals.risk: The risk is that it reads as unfinished to operators expecting a rich harvest scene. The counter: every element present is load-bearing. The empty upper field is not absence — it is the condition that makes the lyric legible without a dimming band that fights the scene. The single contrast (warm stalk against dark sky) is the only contrast. If a reviewer wants more, I will ask what the more would mean, not add it.

disputes.objection: The unison sway is the tell — when every stalk moves in the same wind direction simultaneously as a 'congregational breath,' the field stops being a field and becomes a stage curtain, and no one in a real harvest has ever felt that; the drama is purchased at the cost of the evidence. The linen grain at 3% static over the full frame is texture as costume, not texture as process — it sits on top of the scene like a filter someone applied after the fact, which is exactly what I fight. And the warm-band sky expansion keyed to vocal is the scene performing emotion rather than the scene receiving it — the sky should not be a mood ring for the singer.
disputes.concession: The decision to run the warm band on the vocal channel rather than the swell channel is a real timing judgment — a voice deserves the sky, not the wind — and that editorial instinct is the kind of human choice that survives the work.

disputes.objection: The unison sway — all stalks moving in the same wind direction simultaneously, called 'congregational breath' — is the most culturally loaded editorial decision in any of these proposals, and it goes unnamed as such: whose congregation, whose harvest ritual, whose nave vault is this field leaning into? The proposal reaches for sacred grandeur before asking what tradition that grandeur belongs to, and the linen grain and anamorphic streak are doing the same work — they are borrowing the material vocabulary of a specific photographic and liturgical inheritance without declaring it.
